#  Google Cloud release notes Stay organized with collections  Save and categorize content based on your preferences. 

The following release notes cover the most recent changes over the last 60 days. For a comprehensive list of product-specific release notes, see the [individual product release note pages](https://docs.cloud.google.com/release-notes/all).

You can also see and filter all release notes in the [Google Cloud console](https://console.cloud.google.com/release-notes) or you can programmatically access release notes in [BigQuery](https://console.cloud.google.com/bigquery?p=bigquery-public-data&d=google_cloud_release_notes&t=release_notes&page=table).

To get the latest product updates delivered to you, add the URL of this page to your [feed reader](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_feed_aggregators), or add the [feed URL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/feeds/gcp-release-notes.xml) directly. 

## October 22, 2026

**App Engine standard environment PHP**

Security

All supported versions of [PHP 8.2](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/lifecycle/support-schedule#php) and later are patched. Take immediate protective action by redeploying your resources with updated dependencies.

See [Responding to core PHP vulnerabilities](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/responding-to-core-php-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619) for more information.

**BigQuery**

Feature

The [`AI.TRANSLATE` function](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-ai-translate) lets you translate text strings between languages. `AI.TRANSLATE` supports standard Neural Machine Translation (NMT) workloads and Translation LLM (TLLM) capabilities.

This function is [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) (GA).

**Cloud Run**

Feature

You can configure [Direct VPC ingress for Cloud Run instances](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/vpc-direct-vpc#direct-vpc-instance) ([Preview](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages)). Direct VPC ingress lets Cloud Run instances on a VPC network use their own ephemeral private IP address to communicate with each other and with other resources on the VPC network.

Security

All supported versions of [PHP 8.2](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/runtime-support#php) and later are patched. Take immediate protective action by redeploying your resources with updated dependencies.

See [Responding to core PHP vulnerabilities](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/responding-to-core-php-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619) for more information.

**Cloud Run functions**

Security

All supported versions of [PHP 8.2](https://docs.cloud.google.com/functions/docs/runtime-support#php) and later are patched. Take immediate protective action by redeploying your resources with updated dependencies.

See [Responding to core PHP vulnerabilities](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/responding-to-core-php-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619) for more information.

**Compute Engine**

Feature

You can view how a managed instance group (MIG) distributes its instances across zones and machine types, directly from the MIG's **Monitoring** tab in the Google Cloud console.

For more information, see [Monitor instance distribution in MIGs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups/monitor-instance-distribution).

**Data Studio**

Feature

You can connect Data Studio to a BigQuery Graph or query a graph by using a custom SQL query in the BigQuery connector, which imports graph measures as metrics that you can use in your reports. For more information, see [Connect to Google BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/connect-to-google-bigquery#connect-to-a-bigquery-table-or-view).

**Firestore**

Feature

[Data modification language (DML) operations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/pipeline/dml) are generally available ([GA](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages)). Added support for [`insert`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/pipeline/stages/output/insert) and [`upsert`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/pipeline/stages/output/upsert).

**Gemini Enterprise**

Feature

**Gemini Enterprise: Single-user quota limits**

Gemini Enterprise administrators can configure single-user quota limits on the **Usage & Spending > Usage** page in the Google Cloud console to prevent an individual user from using all of an edition's shared subscription quota pool. You can enable a single-user quota limit and set a quota multiplier for each edition and location across the Gemini Enterprise Standard, Gemini Enterprise Plus, and Gemini Enterprise Standard Emerging Market editions.

This feature is generally available (GA). For more information, see:

  * [Single-user quota limits](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/quotas-and-overages#single-user-quota-limits)
  * [Configure a single-user quota limit](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/feature-usage#configure-single-user-quota-limit)
  * [Configure overages](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-overages#configure-single-user-quota-limit)



**Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for bare metal**

Announcement

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for bare metal 1.34.1000-gke.111 is now available for download. To upgrade, see [Upgrade clusters](https://docs.cloud.google.com/release-notes/how-to/upgrade). Google Distributed Cloud for bare metal 1.34.1000-gke.111 runs on Kubernetes v1.34.7-gke.200.

After a release, it takes approximately 7 to 14 days for the version to become available for installations or upgrades with the GKE On-Prem API clients: the Google Cloud console, the gcloud CLI, and Terraform.

If you use a third-party storage vendor, check the listing of our previously-qualified [storage partners](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/enterprise/docs/resources/partner-storage).

Feature

The following features were introduced in 1.34.1000-gke.111:

  * Fixed an issue in clusters using bundled BGP load balancing where control plane upgrades or configuration updates could cause up to 20 seconds of API server connection failures while a control plane node restarted. After the fix, failover to a healthy control plane node completes in approximately 4 seconds. 
  * Fixed an issue where the `NodePool` controller prematurely updated `Status.ManagedFields` on partial reconciliation failures, causing removed taints and labels to remain stranded on affected nodes. 



Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.34.1000-gke.111:

  * Fixed vulnerabilities listed in [Vulnerability fixes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/distributed-cloud/bare-metal/docs/vulnerabilities).
  * Fixed `BareMetalMachine` conditions during maintenance mode transitions. 
  * Fixed an issue where updating control plane configurations caused multiple API servers to restart simultaneously, leading to transient control plane unavailability. 



**Looker**

Announcement

**Looker 26.22** will roll out to Looker (original) instances on the following schedule:

  * Expected Looker (original) deployment start: **Monday, October 26, 2026**
  * Expected Looker (original) final deployment and download available: **Monday, November 9, 2026**



The Looker 26.22 rollout for Looker (Google Cloud core) will be announced separately.

Looker 26.22 is expected to include the following changes, features, and fixes.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where table column options menus and search boxes appeared behind drill dialogs, which prevented users from interacting with them. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where configuring a LookML model could trigger unnecessary derived table rebuilds. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where the **Show filters** option was displayed on dashboard tiles that failed to load data in view mode. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where drilling into results that were filtered by string dimensions that contained backslashes returned zero rows. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where pivoted queries in SQL Runner could fail to render or re-pivot unexpectedly. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where the **View (Expanded / Full Screen)** option appeared in the tile action menu on embedded dashboards in view mode. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where custom visualization tiles were truncated in dashboard PDF exports when the **Expand tables to show all rows** option was enabled. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

Table row group subtotals are now displayed only for sum and count measures. For other measure types (such as `averages` and `count distinct`) and table calculations, subtotals are now left blank rather than displaying an inaccurate summed value.

Fixed

The System Activity `query_metrics` Explore now records connection acquisition time (`acquire_connection`) for queries that are canceled while waiting in the connection pool.

Fixed

Conversational Analytics `DELETE` endpoints now return `HTTP 404 Not Found` instead of `HTTP 204 No Content` when you attempt to delete nonexistent resources.

Fixed

The System Activity `query_metrics` Explore has been updated to accurately record model initialization time for models that are loaded from cache.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where adding a new series to a categorical chart, such as adding a new pivot value, could cause category bars to appear ungrouped. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed in the TypeScript and JavaScript SDKs where calling methods that have only optional parameters without passing an empty object could result in compilation or runtime errors. This feature now performs as expected.

## October 21, 2026

**Apigee X**

Announcement

**Apigee Emulator**

### Apigee Emulator v2.0.2

On October 21, 2026, we released Apigee Emulator version 2.0.2.

This release upgrades the Apigee Emulator runtime to Java 21 (Eclipse Temurin JRE 21) to align local proxy development and policy execution with the production Apigee runtime, while keeping the embedded Apache Cassandra datastore pinned to Java 8. It also addresses 46 security vulnerabilities across Netty, Jackson, Apache Log4j, BouncyCastle, Apache CXF, Eclipse Jetty, and the embedded Cassandra Go standard library health-check binary.

The emulator image is available at [Artifact Registry](https://console.cloud.google.com/artifacts/docker/apigee-release/us/gcr.io/hybrid%2Fapigee-emulator).

To upgrade, update the emulator version in your Cloud Code for VS Code settings to `2.0.2`. See [Manage the Apigee Emulator](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/local-development/vscode/manage-apigee-emulator#choose_the_emulator_version) for details.

Feature

**Apigee Emulator**

#### Changed in this release

  * Upgraded the Apigee Emulator runtime JVM to Eclipse Temurin JRE 21 (`21.0.12.1.0+1-0`, from JRE 11 `11.0.31+11`), adding JVM 21 compatibility flags (`-Djava.security.manager=allow` and `--add-opens` module flags) for `JavaCallout`, JavaScript (Rhino), and Python (Jython) policies while keeping the embedded Apache Cassandra `4.0.19` datastore pinned to Eclipse Temurin JRE 8.
  * Upgraded Netty to `4.1.137.Final` (from `4.1.135.Final`) and updated `netty-tcnative-boringssl-static` and `netty-tcnative-classes` to `2.0.81.Final` (from `2.0.77.Final`).
  * Upgraded Jackson (`jackson-core`, `jackson-databind`, and `jackson-dataformat-yaml`) to `2.21.7` (from `2.18.6` and `2.19.2`) and `jackson-annotations` to `2.21`.
  * Upgraded shaded Apache Log4j (`log4j-api` and `log4j-core`) in `ConfigUtil.jar` to `2.25.5` (from `2.17.1` and `2.25.4`).
  * Upgraded BouncyCastle (`bcprov-jdk18on`, `bcpkix-jdk18on`, and `bcutil-jdk18on`) to `1.85` (from `1.84`).
  * Upgraded Apache CXF (`cxf-*`) to `3.6.12` (from `3.5.11`).
  * Upgraded gRPC to `1.82.3` (from `1.62.2`), Protobuf (`protobuf-java` and `protobuf-java-util`) to `4.33.6` (from `3.25.5`), and Guava to `33.5.0-jre` (from `33.4.8-jre`).
  * Removed unused `org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-*` (`9.4.58.v20250814`) and `commons-collections:commons-collections` (`3.2.2`) JARs from the emulator distribution.
  * Refreshed the Cassandra base image to pick up Go standard library `1.27.0` (from `1.25.11`) in the embedded `/opt/apigee/ready` health-check binary.

**Apigee hybrid**

Announcement

### v1.15.9

On October 21, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.15.9.

  * For information on upgrading, see [Upgrading Apigee hybrid to version v1.15.9](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/hybrid/v1.15/upgrade).
  * For information on new installations, see [The big picture](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/hybrid/v1.15/big-picture).

**Note:** This is a patch release: The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch via the Helm chart automatically updates the images. No manual image changes are typically needed. For information on container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see [Apigee release process](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/release/apigee-release-process#apigee-hybrid-container-images).

Fixed

#### Fixed in this release

Bug ID | Description  
---|---  
**573622417** | **Fixed an issue where`apigee-ingressgateway` forwarded the `x-envoy-decorator-operation` header to upstream runtime and target backends.**  
**571378258** | **The`apigee-redis` container now uses the Valkey engine (version 8.1.10). The RESP2 wire protocol and `redis-server` and `redis-cli` binary names are unchanged.**  
**568860869** | **Fixed an issue in the`RegularExpressionProtection` policy where patterns starting and ending with `.*` whose middle section contained regular expression syntax were matched as literal text instead of regular expressions.**  
**565072374** | **Fixed an issue where`VerifyJWT` policies using a JWKS `uriRef` could return `steps.jwt.NoMatchingPublicKey` on the first request after the 5-minute JWKS cache TTL expired when the identity provider rotated keys. The cache now refreshes synchronously upon expiration.**  
**535395491** | **Extension Processor (`ext_proc`) denials now return the status and body that the policy or FaultRule produced, instead of always returning HTTP `500`.**  
**524115876** | **Fixed an intermittent HTTP`400` error in the `OASValidation` policy's strict parameter validation that rejected valid requests under load.**  
**519729209** | **Fixed a SAML XML Signature Wrapping vulnerability in the`ValidateSAMLAssertion` policy.**  
**502231886** | **Fixed an issue where the`SanitizeUserPrompt` and `SanitizeModelResponse` policies failed to extract content using default source templates when the `<Source>` element was omitted and `<IgnoreUnresolvedVariables>` was set to `false`.**  
**432315283** | **Fixed an issue where changes to a multi-certificate truststore's trust anchors required a Message Processor restart when`features.truststore.multi_cert_bundle.enabled` was toggled at runtime; the outbound `SSLContext` now rebuilds automatically.**  
**428750492** | **Removed the`required` validation constraint on the `strategy` and `stages` fields in the `ApigeeDeployment` CRD.**

**BigQuery**

Feature

The [`AI.CHUNK_DOCUMENT` function](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-ai-chunk-document) is a table-valued function that splits unstructured documents into semantically coherent text chunks optimized for vector embeddings and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflows.

This function is [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) (GA).

**Buildpacks**

Feature

Patch updates to [PHP runtimes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/flexible/lifecycle/support-schedule#php) are available on `google-22` and `google-24` tags: `8.5.12`, `8.4.27`, `8.3.36`, and `8.2.35`. Take immediate action to protect your PHP workloads by rebuilding your workloads with updated dependencies. **Cloud Billing**

Feature

**SKU attributes and granular usage units in pricing data export (Preview)**

SKU attributes and granular usage units are now available in [Preview](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) in the Cloud Billing [pricing data export to BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/export-data-bigquery-tables/pricing-data).

  * **SKU attributes** : SKU attributes are key-value pairs that describe the SKU. For example, _Key_ : `model_name`, _Value_ : `gemini_2_5_flash`.
  * **Granular usage units** : Granular usage units are the usage unit of the SKU, such as `tokens`.



For more information about these dimensions, see the following:

  * [SKU attributes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/export-data-bigquery-tables/pricing-data#sku_attributes)
  * [Granular usage units](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/export-data-bigquery-tables/pricing-data#sku_granular_usage_units)

**Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform**

Fixed

**CodeMender updates (v0.16.0)**

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  * **Deep scan by default (`cm find`)**: `cm find` now runs a concurrent file-by-file deep scan (`--deep`) by default for higher vulnerability recall across repositories. To run a single-session quick scan instead, pass the `--quick` flag (`cm find --quick`). `cm stats` now breaks down scan usage by mode (`--deep`, `--quick`, and `--diff`).
  * **Pre-flight health checks (`cm health`)**: Added the `cm health` command (with `--json`, `--strict`, and `--timeout` flags) to verify credentials, configuration, endpoint reachability, and project authorization before running scans.
  * **Expanded file discovery** : `cm find` now scans `.hh`, `.hxx`, `.inl`, and `.ipp` C++ headers, extensionless scripts with supported language shebangs (`python`, `node`, `ruby`, and `php`), nested `build/`, `target/`, `obj/`, and `bin/` source directories, and production code under `spec/`, `locale/`, and `i18n/`.
  * **Bug fixes** : 
    * Restricted `cm verify` file writes to `.exploit/` inside the project root and skipped missing or out-of-scope session artifacts during workspace restore.
    * Capped single-turn file reads at 256 KiB with pagination hints, bounded unified diff generation on large files, and raised `run_command` default and maximum timeouts to 120 seconds and 300 seconds.
    * Fixed an issue where sandboxed sessions could not write tool call entries to `~/.codemender/audit.log`.
    * Updated multi-file `--deep` and `--diff` scans to report `INCOMPLETE` status when one or more file scans fail.



For more information, see the [CodeMender documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/agents/codemender).

## October 20, 2026

**Apigee X**

Announcement

On October 20th, 2026, we began maintenance updates of Apigee instances [configured for maintenance windows](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/system-administration/maintenance-windows).

If you set a preferred window for maintenance for your instance, and your instance version is below **1-18-0-apigee-6** , your instance will be updated to **1-18-0-apigee-6** within the next seven to 21 days. A notification containing the expected date of upgrade will be sent within the next two business days.

Note: Instances that meet either of the following two criteria will **not** be updated: 

  * Your instance has a DNS misconfiguration, as described in [Known Issue 445936920](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/release/known-issues).
  * Your instance uses an Apigee Java Library that has been removed, as described in [Apigee release notes dated October 16, 2025](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/release/release-notes#October_16_2025).



For more information on participating in scheduled maintenance windows, see [Maintenance overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/system-administration/maintenance) and [Manage Apigee instance maintenance windows](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/system-administration/maintenance-windows).

**Cloud SDK**

Breaking

## 590.0.0 (2026-10-20)

### Breaking Changes

  * **(Google Cloud CLI)** Removed the `gcloud-man-pages` component. Use `--help` for full command documentation.
  * **(App Engine)** Removed the `app-engine-grpc` component from the Google Cloud CLI.
  * **(Cloud Build)** Removed the Cloud Build Local Builder component (`cloud-build-local`) from the Google Cloud CLI.



### Google Cloud CLI

  * Updated bundled Python on Linux and Windows, and in the Alpine-based Docker images, to pyOpenSSL 26.4.0 and cryptography 50.0.1. 32-bit Windows uses pyOpenSSL 26.2.0 and cryptography 48.0.1, the newest releases that support it.



### AI

  * Updated `gcloud beta ai endpoints deploy-model` to request automatic resources for Gemini deployments on GDC connected endpoints. 
    * If no replica counts are specified, the minimum replica count defaults to 1 only for `gemini-2.5-flash`.
    * Specifying flags that apply only to dedicated resources, such as `--machine-type` or `--accelerator`, now prints a warning and deploys with dedicated resources.



### Agent Identity

  * Added `gcloud beta agent-identity auth-providers resolve-authorization` command.



### AlloyDB

  * Added `--enable-public-dns` flag to `gcloud beta alloydb instances create|update`.



### Apigee

  * Fixed an issue where `gcloud apigee` commands would fail with an `UnauthorizedRequestError` for users who authenticate using Mutual TLS (mTLS).



### App Engine

  * Updated `gcloud beta app migrate-to-run` to default to the App Engine application's region instead of `us-central1` when neither `--region` nor the `run/region` property is set.



### BigLake

  * Promoted `--federated-catalog-identity-mode` for `gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs create` to GA.
  * Promoted `--federated-catalog-identity-mode` for `gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs update` to GA.
  * Promoted `--metadata-service-directory-name` for `gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs create` to GA.
  * Promoted `--metadata-service-directory-name` for `gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs update` to GA.
  * `federated` value for `--catalog-type` flag of `gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs create` is now supported.



### Certificate Authority Service

  * Added `--filter` flag to `gcloud privateca subordinates list`. The flag is able to allow filtering results based on specified boolean expression.



### Cloud Bigtable

  * Build with 1.26.4 to resolve CVE-2026-39820.



### Cloud Bigtable Emulator

  * Rebuild cbt-emulator for CVE-2026-39820.



### Cloud Dataflow

  * Promoted `gcloud dataflow config-store-settings` to GA.



### Cloud Dataplex

  * Fixed `gcloud dataplex dbt metadata-jobs create` so that dbt resources whose names contain a dot, such as tests on a model with a decimal version, are no longer rejected by the import job.
  * Fixed `gcloud dataplex dbt metadata-jobs create` so that two dbt resources that map to the same Dataplex entry ID no longer fail the whole import job. The first is imported and a warning names the other.



### Cloud IAM

  * Added `--vendor-type` flag to `gcloud iam workforce-pools providers create-oidc`, `create-saml`, `update-oidc`, and `update-saml` commands.



### Cloud Resource Manager

  * Promoted `gcloud resource-manager capability-configs` to GA.
  * Promoted `gcloud resource-manager boundary-configs` to GA.
  * Promoted `gcloud resource-manager boundaries` to GA.



### Cloud Run

  * Added `--dry-run` flag to `gcloud beta run domain-mappings create` to validate a domain mapping, including whether the domain is available, without creating it.



### Cloud SQL

  * Added `POSTGRES_19` to `--database-version` flag of `gcloud sql instances create` and `gcloud sql instances patch`.
  * Added `--no-replication-lag-max-seconds-for-recreate` flag to `gcloud beta sql instances patch` to disable recreating a lagging MySQL read replica.
  * Updated 'cloud-sql-proxy' packaged component to use 2.26.2 of the Cloud SQL Proxy.



### Cloud Spanner

  * Improved error output when `gcloud spanner cli` runs an incompatible `spanner-cli` binary found on `PATH` instead of the `spanner-cli` component; users are now directed to install the component.



### Cloud Workstations

  * Added `enable-automatic-failover` to `--boost-config` flag in `gcloud beta workstations configs create` and `gcloud beta workstations configs update`.



### Compute Engine

  * Added `compute instance-templates export` command to all release tracks.
  * Removed WORKLOAD_IDENTITY choise in `--identity-type` flag.
  * Promoted `--instance-flexibility-policy` flag and min CPU platform and disk overrides to GA for `gcloud compute instance-groups managed create` and `update`.
  * Added `compute instance-templates import` command to all release tracks.



### Database Migration

  * Added `--failback` flag to `gcloud database-migration migration-jobs promote` command to promote a migration job from destination back to source during the FAILBACK phase.



### GKE Hub

  * Promoted `--view`, `--memberships`, `--filter`, and `--sort-by` flags on `gcloud container fleet|hub config-management describe` command to `GA`.

  * Updated `gcloud container fleet|hub memberships register` to allow skipping the Connect agent installation on non-GKE clusters via the `--no-install-connect-agent` flag.




### Kubernetes Engine

  * Added the `reservedSystemCpus` kubelet config option to the `gcloud container clusters create`, `gcloud container node-pools create`, and `gcloud container node-pools update` commands. This option specifies the list of CPUs reserved for host system services.
  * Added `ltsc2025` option to `--windows-os-version` flag of `gcloud container node-pools create` and `gcloud container node-pools update` to create or update Windows node pools using the Windows Server 2025 (LTSC2025) image.
  * Updated default kubectl to 1.35.9.
  * Additional kubectl versions: 
    * 1.31.14
    * 1.32.13
    * 1.33.13
    * 1.34.12
    * 1.35.9
    * 1.36.5
    * 1.37.1
  * Allowed `--num-nodes=0` for `gcloud container clusters create` to create a cluster without a default node pool on GKE versions that support it. Flags that only configure the default node pool, such as `--machine-type` and `--enable-autoscaling`, can't be used with `--num-nodes=0`.



### Network Connectivity

  * Added `--purpose` flag to `gcloud network-connectivity internal-ranges create` to specify the purpose of the internal range.



### Network Security

  * Promoted `--wildfire-analysis-profile` flag of `gcloud network-security security-profile-groups create` and `gcloud network-security security-profile-groups update` commands to GA.
  * Promoted `gcloud network-security security-profiles wildfire-analysis` command group and its `create`, `delete`, `describe`, `list` and `update` commands to GA.
  * Promoted `add-submission-rule`, `delete-submission-rule`, `add-inline-cloud-analysis-rule` and `delete-inline-cloud-analysis-rule` commands of `gcloud network-security security-profiles wildfire-analysis` to GA.



### Service Extensions

  * Created a new set of commands for `gcloud service-extensions extension-bindings` (alpha and beta).
  * Added `gcloud beta service-extensions cdn-edge-extensions` command group to manage `CdnEdgeExtension` resources.



Subscribe to these release notes at <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/google-cloud-sdk-announce>.

**Cloud Workstations**

Feature

Cloud Workstations supports automatic failover for [boost configurations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/workstations/docs/boost-workstation#automatic-failover) in [Preview](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages). When you enable automatic failover, Cloud Workstations automatically provisions a workstation VM using the boost configuration if Compute Engine lacks capacity for the default machine type during startup.

**Gemini Enterprise**

Feature

**Gemini Enterprise: Antigravity Enterprise Gateway support**

Antigravity Enterprise Gateway lets organizations route model inference requests from the Antigravity app, Antigravity CLI, and Antigravity for IDEs through a centralized enterprise gateway before forwarding them to Google Cloud. This deployment enables organizations to inspect and audit model traffic, enforce custom security and network egress policies, and authenticate developers through a gateway API key without requiring individual Google Account sign-in.

Requests routed through Antigravity Enterprise Gateway use a centralized Google Cloud service account and are billed on a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) consumption basis through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. This deployment model doesn't use your Gemini Enterprise seat-based subscription quotas (such as included Standard or Plus monthly allowances). You can't use a gateway and sign in with a Google Account at the same time. If you want to use your included subscription quota instead, disable the enterprise gateway and sign in with your Google Account.

This feature is generally available (GA).

For more information, see:

  * [Deploy Antigravity Enterprise Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/ai-developer-tools/deploy-enterprise-gateway)
  * [Connect Antigravity to an Enterprise Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/ai-developer-tools/connect-enterprise-gateway).



Breaking

**Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 2.5 Pro discontinued in Canada and Japan**

Gemini 2.5 Pro has been discontinued for in-country Gemini Enterprise app deployments in Canada and Japan. Agents and chat sessions in these regions that previously used Gemini 2.5 Pro automatically switch to in-country Gemini 3.5 Flash.

Gemini 2.5 Pro remains available in the `global`, `us`, and `eu` regions.

For more information, see [Data residency for Gemini Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations) and [Manage web app features](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/manage-web-app-features).

This issue has been resolved. You can upgrade your cluster control plane to the following versions to fix the issue for `ubuntu_containerd` and older `cos_containerd` node pools:

**Spanner**

Feature

Spanner supports approximate aggregate functions for both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. These functions produce statistical estimates of distinct counts, allowing you to compute results faster and save resources on large datasets compared to exact aggregation.

For more information, see approximate aggregate functions ([GoogleSQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/approximate_aggregate_functions) and [PostgreSQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/postgresql/functions#approximate-aggregate)), [HyperLogLog++ functions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/hll_functions), and [Sketches](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/sketches).

Feature

**Transcript separation for chat**

You can now configure Google Cloud CCaaS to deliver a separate transcript file for each participant segment in a chat, instead of one combined transcript per session. Under **Settings > Chat > Chat Transcript**, select **Per Segment** in **Transcript Separation** to generate individual transcript files for each agent, virtual agent, or supervisor who joins the chat—helpful for identifying which participant handled each part of a transferred or escalated conversation. Your consumers still receive a single, full-chat transcript regardless of this setting.

For more information, see [Chat transcripts and chat history](https://docs.cloud.google.com/contact-center/ccai-platform/docs/chat-transcripts-and-chat-history).

By default, this capability is inactive. Contact Google Cloud Support to turn it on for your instance.

Feature

**Campaign-based scheduled callbacks**

Agents can now schedule a callback during an outbound campaign call. The callback belongs to the campaign, not to an individual agent, and the dialer calls the consumer back in the time slot they chose. Administrators set slot length, capacity, booking window, and expiry for each campaign, and supervisors can track upcoming, completed, and expired callbacks from the campaign list.

For more information, see [Campaign management](https://docs.cloud.google.com/contact-center/ccai-platform/docs/campaign-management).

Fixed

This release addresses the following issues:

  * Fixed an issue where direct access point (DAP) greeting messages played twice when a call was deflected to an internal phone number due to queue overcapacity.

  * Fixed an issue where session metadata for top-level menu paths and selected menus was incorrectly displayed in English instead of the user's configured language.

  * Fixed an issue where a failed Salesforce lookup was incorrectly treated as having no matches, which resulted in the creation of duplicate records.

  * Fixed an issue where inbound transfer restrictions remained in force even after being hidden in the administrator interface, causing queues to become silently unreachable for transfers.

  * Fixed an issue where hold music continued to play throughout a call recording after a warm transfer was completed.

  * Fixed an issue where outbound virtual agent audio was prematurely truncated during multi-message turns.

  * Fixed an issue where the **Real-time Monitoring Queues** report didn't accurately count skill-matched agents for skills-based queues, often displaying zero available agents despite their availability.

  * Fixed an issue where calls deflected to an external phone number after entering a queue were incorrectly recorded as abandoned by the customer.

  * Fixed an issue where the credit card tokenizer was missing from the **SmartActions** menu during outbound callback calls.

  * Fixed an issue where mandatory call dispositions were discarded if an agent's voice connection dropped but their session remained active.

  * Fixed an issue where the text resize menu in the chat widget wasn't scrollable at 400% browser zoom, which prevented users from accessing all available text size options.

  * Fixed an issue where the system incorrectly prevented saving automatic call redirection settings when the target was a virtual agent-operated queue.

  * Fixed an issue where duplicate call records were created for a single inbound call, causing incorrect wait times to appear in the real-time queue view.

  * Fixed an issue where empty data attributes caused an error in the agent interface during call connections.

  * Fixed an issue where the **Transfer Restrictions** destination picker provided no feedback when a queue was ineligible, making it indistinguishable from a typo or search error.

  * Fixed an issue where incoming calls were rejected with a SIP 603 error due to high database latency and connection timeouts.

  * Fixed an issue where the documentation for the Apps API and call session metadata schema didn't define the top-level `parentId` and `finishReason` fields.

  * Fixed an issue where certain inbound call failures were incorrectly reported as a busy signal.

  * Fixed an issue where the event processor service crashed during scaling or rebalancing of the system.

  * Fixed an issue where the conversation ID was missing from chat events during active sessions.

  * Fixed an issue where report exports didn't download or remained stuck in a processing state indefinitely.

  * Fixed an issue where agents could transfer calls to queues that were already closed if their transfer list was loaded while the queue was still open.

  * Fixed an issue where queued chats were assigned to agents after the end-user had become unresponsive without being prompted to check in.

  * Fixed an issue where voice calls cold-transferred to an over-capacity queue generated duplicate reporting records and incorrect queue wait times if the callback leg failed.

  * Fixed an issue where direct inbound calls deflected to voicemail during after-hours played three separate audio prompts sequentially.

  * Fixed an issue where a single call was simultaneously assigned to two different agents if the pickup coincided with the cascade timer expiry.

  * Fixed an issue where direct inbound calls weren't projected to agents in a breakthrough-enabled status if another call was already waiting in their queue.

  * Fixed an issue where a gray empty area appeared below the chat container in the agent adapter when the iframe width was narrower than 449px.

  * Fixed an issue where several Kubernetes and Google Cloud service accounts were granted overly broad permissions, which could have allowed for unauthorized privilege escalation.

  * Fixed an issue where an agent's status sequence was recorded in the incorrect order following a brief connection loss during an active chat.

  * Fixed an issue where selecting a contact during a native campaign call didn't automatically open the corresponding record in the CRM.

  * Fixed an issue where AI-generated Smart Disposition suggestions were inconsistently displayed for outbound calls during the wrap-up period.

  * Fixed an issue where call recordings became distorted or garbled when multiple holds were placed during a call.

  * Fixed an issue where audio uploads were accepted based on the file extension rather than the actual file content, which caused call disconnections when incompatible formats were played.

  * Fixed an issue where the call duration timer in the external call adapter didn't match the **In-call** status timer in the agent desktop for inbound calls.

  * Fixed an issue where the sentiment score was incorrectly displayed in the call adapter for calls escalated from a virtual agent, even when the **Sentiment Analysis** setting was disabled.

  * Fixed an issue where duplicate reporting rows were generated for call and wrap-up durations due to concurrent system events.

  * Fixed an issue where agents couldn't sign in or refresh their status if their account was linked to a deleted or unknown status.

  * Fixed an issue where the Manager API documentation for agent activity logs omitted 17 chat routing and activity values, leading to incomplete reporting data for customers.

  * Fixed an issue where IVR custom callback numbers for certain international regions, including Norway and Denmark, were incorrectly dialed with a +1 prefix.

  * Fixed an issue where metadata for calls deflected between virtual agent assignment and connection wasn't exported to the Cloud Storage bucket.

  * Fixed an issue where virtual agent to human chat escalations experienced delays of up to 300 seconds during agent assignment.

  * Fixed an issue where the **Answer** button didn't appear for dial-by-extension calls when other calls were already waiting in an agent's queue.

  * Fixed an issue where a supervisor's name didn't appear in the chat widget when joining a conversation using the monitor then barge workflow.

  * Fixed an issue where ending a chat session in one browser tab didn't automatically close the chat widget in other open tabs.

Announcement

**Advanced reporting dashboards prerelease notes 6.16**

Here are the pre-release notes for updates to the advanced reporting dashboards and other reporting in CCAI Platform. When we release these updates, we expect the new capabilities to be as shown here.

**Important:** The next version of the advanced reporting dashboards could be greater than 6.16.

Fixed

This release addresses the following issues:

  * Fixed an issue where the **Agent Performance** tile on the **Real-time Agent Monitoring** dashboard executed redundant database queries during auto-refreshes.

  * Updated advanced reporting filter prompts so they behave consistently across all dashboards and display the complete list of configured values:

    * List-backed filters now open directly into a searchable list on the first click.

    * Dropdowns that previously returned empty or partial lists now display the full configured list, including **Agent Name** , **Agent Email** , **Agent Custom ID** , **Agent Teams** , **Location** , **Language** , **Answered By** , and **Projection Result**.

    * **Disposition Codes** and **Disposition List** filters now display the codes configured for your instance.

    * **Agent Teams** and **Team Name** filters now match agents in any of their assigned teams.

    * Configuration renames (**Queue Group** , **Queue** , **Agent Team** , **Disposition Code** , **Location** , **Role** , and **Skill**) now appear in filter dropdowns within 30 minutes instead of up to six hours.

    * The **Projecting** filter on the live **Queued** dashboards is now clearable, so you can reset it to show all queued interactions, and offers only **Yes**.

    * Fields without a predefined list of values (such as consumer phone numbers and ID fields) now display a plain text box with an operator so you can type a value directly.

    * **Call Status** and **Deflection Type** filters now display values that existed in the data but were previously missing from the list.

    * **Channel** now reports a value on the live **Voice** and **Chat** dashboards, and on historical **Chat** dashboards, for interaction types that previously appeared blank (including internal, API-initiated, campaign, UCaaS, callback, and extension calls).

    * On the **Agent Audit** dashboard, the **Change Details** table now displays its timestamp column and sorts it correctly.

    * Consumer phone number filters now accept a single value instead of multiple values. Saved filters or links that pass multiple numbers apply only one.

    * On the **Missed Interactions** dashboards, the **Activity Status** column and filter are renamed to **Projection Result**.

    * Actor values describing who answered, ended, or disconnected an interaction are now standardized as **Human Agent** , **Virtual Agent** , **End User** , and **System**. Saved filters, Looks, and schedules that used the previous wording must be reselected.




**Google Kubernetes Engine**

Change

For GKE Standard CPU node pools, GKE can now upgrade nodes by updating the existing Compute Engine VM in place, instead of deleting the VM and creating a new one. Because the node keeps its underlying VM, it also keeps its compute capacity during the upgrade. This lowers the risk that a node upgrade fails or stalls because resources aren't available.

To enable this type of upgrade, use [surge upgrades with the `maxUnavailable` field](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-pool-upgrade-strategies#max-unavailable) set to a value greater than 0. For more details about when GKE reuses the same Compute Engine instance, including exceptions, see [maxUnavailable: GKE makes an existing node unavailable to recreate it](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-pool-upgrade-strategies#max-unavailable).

This change applies to all GKE versions. To opt out, contact [Cloud Customer Care](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/getting-support).

## October 15, 2026

**Apigee Edge for Private Cloud**

Announcement

Released Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

Designated Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.00 a long-term support (LTS) release: 18 months of full support ending April 2028, then 18 months of maintenance ending October 2029. After October 2029, 4.54.00.00 receives no software updates, security mitigations, or technical support.

Installing a later 4.54 minor release or patch does not change those dates. To extend the support lifecycle, upgrade to the next LTS release.

For the support lifecycle phases, release cadences, and version numbering, see [Apigee Edge for Private Cloud release and lifecycle policy](https://docs.apigee.com/release/private-cloud-release-lifecycle-policy).

Announcement

This release replaces Java 8 with Java 17 and Java 21, removes the Classic UI and the `apigee-sso` component, and updates the bundled Cassandra, Postgres, OpenLDAP, ZooKeeper, Qpid Broker-J, Nginx, and Consul versions. These changes are not backward-compatible.

For the 4.54.00 versions and the 4.53.01 versions they replace, see [Supported software and supported versions](https://docs.apigee.com/release/supported-software).

Before upgrading, read [Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/changes-privatecloud-45400), then [Update Apigee Edge 4.53.00 or 4.53.01 to 4.54.00](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/update-apigee-edge-4530x-45400) or [New installation overview](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/installation-overview). For known issues, see [Known issues with Edge for Private Cloud](https://docs.apigee.com/release/known-issues#private-cloud-known-issues).

Announcement

Replaced the Classic UI (`edge-ui`) with the [New Edge UI](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/new-edge-ui) (`edge-management-ui`).

The New Edge UI is the only management UI in 4.54.00 and is installed by default. Deployments running the Classic UI must transition to it before upgrading. Custom Classic UI properties do not carry over automatically. The default port also changes from `9000` to `3001`, configurable with `conf_uebe_port`, so firewall rules and load balancer target ports that point at `9000` fail until they are updated.

For the migration steps and the supported feature list, see [Migrate to the New Edge UI](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/migrate-ui) and [What features are supported?](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/new-edge-ui#features).

Breaking

In deployments with Apigee SSO enabled, an integrated OIDC identity broker in `apigee-openldap` replaces the standalone `apigee-sso` component and Apache Tomcat 9.0.x. Before upgrading, take a complete and validated LDAP backup; existing `apigee-sso` configurations do not migrate automatically. Deployments not using Apigee SSO require no action.

For migration prerequisites, validation checks, and rollback constraints, see [Option 2: Upgrade UI (with Apigee SSO)](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/update-apigee-edge-4530x-45400#upgrade-ui-with-apigee-sso).

Breaking

4.54.00 runs Java in mixed mode: Java 17 for Cassandra and ZooKeeper, Java 21 for the Management Server, Message Processor, Router, and Qpid Broker-J. Both Oracle JDK and OpenJDK are supported at those versions.

Oracle JDK 8 and OpenJDK 8 are no longer supported.

API proxies with custom JavaCallout policies or custom resource JARs can break on Java 21. For details, see [Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/changes-privatecloud-45400).

Change

Upgraded Nginx on the Edge Router to 1.30.0.

If you are upgrading from Nginx 1.20.x, see [Nginx 1.30 changes in Apigee Edge 4.54.00](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/nginx-45400) for the full list of changes.

Change

Changed the TLS defaults on Message Processors to the Java 21 cryptographic baseline.

Message Processors run on Java 21, which enables TLS 1.3 by default ([JEP 332](https://openjdk.org/jeps/332)) and prefers it for outbound backend connections, falling back to TLS 1.2. No configuration change is required if your target servers and load balancers negotiate TLS 1.3, or negotiate TLS 1.2 with forward-secret (ECDHE) cipher suites.

Java 21 also disables the non-forward-secret static RSA key-exchange suites (`TLS_RSA_*`). If you have overridden `conf_http_HTTPTransport.ssl.cipher.suites.whitelist` or `conf_message-processor-communication_local.http.ssl.ciphers` with static RSA suites only, backend calls fail with `no cipher suites in common` and the Router cannot complete a TLS handshake with the Message Processor. Replace the `TLS_RSA_*` entries with modern cipher suites and restart the Message Processor.

For the remediation path, see [Legacy backend requirements and remediation](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/changes-privatecloud-45400#legacy-tls-remediation).

Feature

Added Basic authentication to the New Edge UI, which lets you sign in without configuring an identity provider.

The [New Edge UI](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/new-edge-ui) supports Basic authentication without additional configuration. You can also configure Apigee SSO, or an external identity provider such as SAML or OIDC. This feature is generally available in 4.54.00.

Feature

Added automated pre-flight validation checks to `apigee-setup` and `apigee-service`, which surface environment configuration problems before a component is installed.

This feature is generally available in 4.54.00.

Security

Fixed multiple security vulnerabilities in Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

These fixes ship as part of the component upgrades in this release; see [Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/changes-privatecloud-45400).

Change

Changed the default garbage collector on Message Processors to the Garbage-First garbage collector.

Message Processors set `useG1GC=true` and `useStringDeduplication=true` by default in 4.54.00. In 4.53.01 neither was set by default. To configure garbage collection, see [Configure the garbage collector for Message Processors](https://docs.apigee.com/private-cloud/v4.54.00/configuring-gc-message-processors-4.54).

Feature

Feature

This feature lets you define an alias for an expression in the `SELECT` clause of a SQL query and immediately reference that alias within the same `SELECT` list or in the `WHERE` clause of the same query block.

Deprecated

We are deprecating the emotion label response in the API. Going forward, the API will return `UNKNOWN` for all emotion related labels.

## October 14, 2026

**Anti Money Laundering AI**

Announcement

New minor engine version released for the commercial line of business within the `v004.011` version line (`aml-commercial.default.v004.011.202610-000`). This version extends support for the major engine version and includes no significant changes compared to the previous minor version.

**Apigee hybrid**

Announcement

### v1.16.11

On October 14, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.16.11.

  * For information on upgrading, see [Upgrading Apigee hybrid to version v1.16.11](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/hybrid/v1.16/upgrade).
  * For information on new installations, see [The big picture](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/hybrid/v1.16/big-picture).

**Note:** This is a patch release: The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch via the Helm chart automatically updates the images. No manual image changes are typically needed. For information on container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see [Apigee release process](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/release/apigee-release-process#apigee-hybrid-container-images).

Fixed

#### Fixed in this release

Bug ID | Description  
---|---  
**565072374** | **Fixed an issue where`VerifyJWT` policies using a JWKS `uriRef` could return `steps.jwt.NoMatchingPublicKey` on the first request after the 5-minute JWKS cache TTL expired when the identity provider rotated keys. The cache now refreshes synchronously upon expiration.**  
**556680325** | **Fixed a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in URL host validation for the`SemanticCacheLookup` policy.**  
**535395491** | **Extension Processor (`ext_proc`) denials now return the status and body that the policy or FaultRule produced, instead of always returning HTTP `500`.**  
**513032450** | **Fixed an issue where`apigee-connect-agent` control-plane connections could hang for up to 2 hours when silently dropped by a network intermediary by restoring a 15-second TCP keep-alive.**  
**502540992** | **Fixed an issue where the`SemanticCacheLookup` policy was incompatible with Vertex AI Vector Search Private Service Connect (PSC) endpoints by adding gRPC transport support via `<PrivateServiceConnect><GrpcEndpoint>`.**  
**492042425** | **Fixed an issue in the`LLMTokenQuota` policy where operation-level token quota values configured on an API product were not applied at runtime, causing product-level quota values to be enforced instead.**

**Application Integration**

Security

An Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the `AuthConfig` validation and integration execution runtime in Application Integration versions prior to August 27, 2026. For more information, see the [GCP-2026-068](https://docs.cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2026-068) security bulletin.

**BigQuery**

Feature

The Apache Hive catalog endpoint in the Lakehouse runtime catalog is now [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) (GA). This integration lets you use the metastore as a serverless, central metadata layer, enabling seamless data sharing and unified querying across Apache Spark, Apache Hive, and BigQuery.

For more information, see [About the Hive catalog endpoint](https://docs.cloud.google.com/lakehouse/docs/about-spark-hive-metastore) and [Set up Spark and Hive with the Lakehouse runtime catalog](https://docs.cloud.google.com/lakehouse/docs/use-spark-hive-metastore).

Feature

Metadata migration from Dataproc Metastore to Lakehouse is now [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) (GA). You can perform a one-time backfill migration or dry run to migrate metadata from a Dataproc Metastore service to an Apache Iceberg REST catalog endpoint or a Hive catalog endpoint using the Google Cloud console, the gcloud CLI, or the REST API.

For more information, see [Migrate metadata from Dataproc Metastore to Lakehouse](https://docs.cloud.google.com/lakehouse/docs/migrate-dataproc-metastore).

Feature

Conversational analytics now lets you [create a conversation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/create-conversations#converse_with_a_data_source_using_the_agents_page) with all of the data sources in multiple projects, or create a conversation with a [dataset](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/create-conversations#datasets). These features are [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) (GA).

Feature

You can publish a [BigQuery Conversational Analytics agent in Gemini Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/create-data-agents#publish-agent-gemini-enterprise). This feature is now [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products/#product-launch-stages) (GA).

Feature

The [`AI.AGG` function](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-ai-agg) now supports the `output_schema` argument, which lets you specify the schema of the function output as a comma-separated list of fields. This feature is [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) (GA).

**Certificate Manager**

Change

Google-managed public SSL certificates signed by [Google Public CA](https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-manager/docs/public-ca) (pki.goog) are gradually transitioning from a 90-day validity period to a 45-day validity period to improve security.

To align with modern industry-wide security standards and promote shorter certificate lifespans, Google-managed public certificates now rotate more frequently. This proactive rotation enhances the overall security posture of load balancers. The transition requires no manual intervention or configuration changes as Certificate Manager automatically manages both issuance and renewal.

For more information, see [Google-managed certificates](https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-manager/docs/core-components#google-managed-certificates) and [Use Google-managed certificates](https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-manager/docs/certificate-manager-best-practices#use_google_managed_certificates).

**Cloud Load Balancing**

Change

Google-managed public SSL certificates signed by [Public Certificate Authority](https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-manager/docs/public-ca) (`pki.goog`) are gradually transitioning from a 90-day validity period to a 45-day validity period to improve security.

To align with modern industry-wide security standards and promote shorter certificate lifespans, Google-managed public certificates signed by Public Certificate Authority now rotate more frequently.

This proactive rotation enhances the overall security posture of load balancers. Transition requires no manual intervention or configuration changes as Google Cloud automatically manages issuance and renewal for both Certificate Manager and Compute Engine SSL certificates.

For more information, see [Renew a Google-managed SSL certificate](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/ssl-certificates/google-managed-certs#renewal).

Feature

Service rate limiting policies are now available in **Preview** for regional internal Application Load Balancers and Secure Web Proxies.

Service rate limiting policies let you maintain service availability among trusted clients that might consume an inordinate amount of resources.

For more information, see the [Service rate limiting overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/srl-policy/service-rate-limiting-overview).

**Cloud SQL for MySQL**

Issue

When you enable the [Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex Universal Catalog)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/dataplex-catalog-integration) integration on a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance created before April 18, 2026, the integration defaults to once a day instead of near real-time.

Near real-time updates upon Knowledge Catalog enablement aren't yet available for all existing instances. A new announcement will be published when this feature becomes available.

**Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL**

Issue

When you enable the [Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex Universal Catalog)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/dataplex-catalog-integration) integration on a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance created before April 18, 2026, the integration defaults to once a day instead of near real-time.

Near real-time updates upon Knowledge Catalog enablement aren't yet available for all existing instances. A new announcement will be published when this feature becomes available.

**Compute Engine**

Feature

**Generally available** : When you reserve capacity by using future reservation requests, you can specify that Compute Engine delivers your reserved capacity as specifically targeted reservations. Specifically targeted reservations help you track and control which Compute Engine instances consume your reserved capacity. For more information, see [About future reservation requests](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/future-reservations-overview).

Feature

**Generally available** : You can increase the size of a Google Cloud Hyperdisk volume that's in multi-writer mode while the volume is attached to multiple instances. Previously, you had to detach the volume from all instances before you could resize it.

For more information, see [Share disks between instances](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/sharing-disks-between-vms) and [Change the size or provisioned performance of a Hyperdisk volume](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/modify-hyperdisks).

**Dataform**

Feature

You can automatically preserve BigQuery data policies and data governance tags (Preview) applied to tables across Dataform executions by enabling the `preserveGovernanceControls` option in your table or workflow configuration. For more information, see [Preserve access controls metadata](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataform/docs/create-tables#preserve-access-controls). This feature is [generally available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) (GA).

**Gemini Enterprise**

Feature

**Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 3.8 Flash regional availability in the United Kingdom**

Gemini 3.8 Flash is generally available (GA) in the United Kingdom.

  * **Location availability** : Supported in the UK (`europe-west2`) in-country region with in-region at-rest data residency (DRZ) and machine learning processing (MLP).
  * **App availability** : Turned on by default in the web app for the UK region. Administrators can manage access with the **Gemini 3.8 Flash** toggle under **Model availability**.



For more information, see [Data residency for Gemini Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations).

Feature

**Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 4 Argon available in Workflow Builder**

Gemini 4 Argon is generally available (GA) for Workflow Builder. Gemini 4 Argon is also available in Workflow Builder workflow agents. Updates take up to a day to appear in workflow agents.

  * **Location availability** : Supported in `global`, `us`, and `eu` multi-regions, with data residency and ML processing support in `us` and `eu`. For more information, see [Data residency for Gemini Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations).
  * **App availability** : Turned off by default. The toggle defaults to on beginning October 27, 2026. For instructions to turn on the model, see [Manage features on the web app](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/manage-web-app-features).



For more information, see [Workflow Builder](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/workflow-builder).

**Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform**

Feature

**Priority PayGo support for Gemini Nano Banana 2.1**

[Priority Pay-as-you-go (PayGo)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/priority-paygo) is available in [General Availability (GA)](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages) for [Gemini Nano Banana 2.1](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/nano-banana-2-1) (`gemini-nano-banana-2.1`) on the `global` endpoint.

Fixed

**CodeMender updates (v0.15.0)**

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  * **Enhanced SARIF 2.1.0 reporting** : Updated `cm report` SARIF output with standardized rule descriptors, severity properties, and repository-relative artifact locations for improved GitHub Code Scanning compatibility.
  * **Model invocation metrics** : Added model invocation tracking to `cm stats --json`, providing total, per-session, and per-turn invocation counts.
  * **Bug fixes** : 
    * Fixed an issue where token usage from completed turns was omitted from session logs during error or cancellation exit paths.



For more information, see the [CodeMender documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/codemender).

Feature

**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is available in Public Preview**

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash from DeepSeek is available as a fully managed model (MaaS) in Model Garden. The model accepts text and image input, targets agentic and coding tasks, and supports a context window of up to 1M tokens.

For more information, see [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/maas/deepseek/deepseek-v41-flash).

**Google Cloud Armor**

Feature

Cloud Armor supports service rate limiting. For more information, see [Cloud Armor and service rate limiting](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/integrating-cloud-armor#service-rate-limiting). This feature is available in Preview.

**Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka**

Feature

Performance of the [Cloud Storage Sink connector](https://docs.cloud.google.com/managed-service-for-apache-kafka/docs/connect-cluster/create-cloud-storage-connector) has been improved. The improvements include reduced out-of-memory errors, higher maximum throughput, and avoiding creating a large number of small files.

**Google Kubernetes Engine**

Change

#### (2026-R44) Version updates

GKE cluster versions have been updated.

**New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.**

The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more information about versioning and upgrades, see [GKE versioning and support](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning) and [About GKE cluster upgrades](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades).

Security

#### (2026-R44) Security updates

This release includes new GKE versions that use updated Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative, incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS versions released since the previous GKE release.

To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated Container-Optimized OS image, see the **Security** release notes for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for each updated Container-Optimized OS image:

GKE version | Container-Optimized OS version | Details  
---|---|---  
1.31.14-gke.2963000 | cos-121-18867-624-8 | [cos-121-18867-624-8 release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m121#cos-121-18867-624-8_)  
1.35.8-gke.1975000 | cos-125-19216-700-23 | [cos-125-19216-700-23 release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-700-23_)  
1.37.1-gke.1697000 | cos-133-19999-44-85 | [cos-133-19999-44-85 release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m133#cos-133-19999-44-85_)  
1.38.0-gke.2884000+preview | cos-133-19999-44-85 | [cos-133-19999-44-85 release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m133#cos-133-19999-44-85_)  
  
Fixed

Fixed an issue in GKE Sandbox where Pods using the Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver could become indefinitely stuck in a `Terminating` state.

To resolve this issue, upgrade your node pools to GKE version 1.37.1-gke.1552000 or later and add the `dev.gvisor.fuse.abort-on-teardown: "true"` annotation to your Pod or Deployment metadata.

For more information, see [About Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver for GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cloud-storage-fuse-csi-driver) and [GKE Known Issues](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting/known-issues).

**Secure Web Proxy**

Feature

Secure Web Proxy supports [service rate limiting policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secure-web-proxy/docs/policies-and-rules-overview#rate-limiting-policies). Use these policies to protect external destinations from traffic overloads and manage the costs of your outbound web traffic.

You can attach a service rate limiting policy to your Secure Web Proxy gateways, whether they use an [authorization policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secure-web-proxy/docs/policies-and-rules-overview#authorization-policies) or a [gateway security policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secure-web-proxy/docs/create-a-policy#gateway-security-policies). For more information, see [Configure service rate limiting policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secure-web-proxy/docs/configure-service-rate-limiting-policies).

This feature is available in [Preview](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages).

**VPC Service Controls**

Feature

**VPC Service Controls feature (Status:[Preview](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages))**: Support for using Workload Identity Federation for GKE in ingress and egress rules to allow access to resources protected by a service perimeter is available in Preview.

You can specify the following Workload Identity Federation for GKE principals in ingress and egress rules:

  * All GKE Pods that use a Kubernetes service account (by service account name or ID)
  * All GKE Pods in a Kubernetes namespace
  * All GKE Pods in a cluster



For more information, see [Configure identity groups and third-party identities in ingress and egress rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/configure-identity-groups) and [Supported identities for ingress and egress rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/supported-identities).

**Cloud Billing**

Feature

**Spend cap budgets are now generally available for a limited set of services**

For [eligible services](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps#eligible-services), you can configure a **spend cap budget** to automatically pause usage when your estimated spend exceeds the budget amount you set. You can manage spend cap budgets in the [Budgets page in the Google Cloud console](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps) and using the [Cloud Billing Budget API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budget-api-spend-cap).

Spend caps are a cost control mechanism. A spend cap is enforced when usage costs exceed your budget target amount. When enforced, any new request to the eligible services, within the specified project, are paused and no further usage costs are accrued until the spend cap is lifted. You can manually lift an enforced spend cap, or wait until the start of the next month when the spend cap is automatically lifted.

Spend caps use _gross, estimated costs_ to trigger the alerts and caps, enforcing a cap much faster than the _actual costs_ are processed and appear on billing reports. Even though faster than reports, the enforcement of spend caps isn't instant and any cost overages are billed as normal.

**More information about spend cap budgets**

For managing spend cap budgets in the Google Cloud console, see:

  * [How spend cap budgets work to help you control spend](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps#how-spend-cap-budgets-work)
  * [Limitations of spend cap budgets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps#limitations)
  * [Configure a spend cap budget](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps#configure-spend-cap)
  * [Lift an enforced spend cap](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps#lift-spend-cap)



For managing spend cap budgets using the Cloud Billing Budget API, see:

  * [Using the Cloud Billing Budget API for spend cap budgets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budget-api-spend-cap)
  * [Spend cap budget concepts and limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budget-api-spend-cap#concepts-limitations)
  * [Create a spend cap budget](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budget-api-spend-cap#create)
  * [Lift an enforced spend cap](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budget-api-spend-cap#lift)
  * [Cloud Billing Budget API REST reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/reference/budget/rest/v1/billingAccounts.budgets)



**Cloud SQL for MySQL**

Feature

[Private Service Connect](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/about-private-service-connect) is now the default private IP connectivity option when you create a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance in a new Google Cloud project. Private Service Connect lets you connect to your instance from multiple Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks across different groups, projects, or organizations, and supports automatic endpoint and DNS record provisioning. When you configure private IP for an instance, you can still choose to use private services access or both connectivity options.

For more information, see [Private IP configuration options](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/private-ip) and [Configure Private Service Connect](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/configure-private-service-connect).

**Cloud Storage**

Feature

Object enrichments is now available in [Preview](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages). When you configure object enrichments, Cloud Storage applies Google's pre-trained machine learning models to eligible images and PDF documents in your buckets and attaches the resulting metadata to your objects as [object contexts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-contexts). You can inspect enrichments on individual objects or query them at scale in BigQuery by using [Storage Insights datasets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/insights/dataset-tables-and-schemas#object-contexts-catalog-schema). For more information, see [About object enrichments](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-enrichments/overview) and [Configure object enrichments](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-enrichments/configure-object-enrichments).

Feature

Object contexts with [extended data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-contexts#extended-data) are available in [Preview](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages). Google services attach these contexts to your objects during automated analysis, such as machine learning labeling. To retrieve a context and its extended data, use the [`viewFullContext`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/objects/viewFullContext) JSON API method.

Feature

Storage Insights datasets include the Object Contexts Catalog view (`object_contexts_catalog_view`), which you can use to analyze object contexts in BigQuery. For more information, see [Object contexts catalog](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/insights/dataset-tables-and-schemas#object-contexts-catalog-schema) and [Analyze object contexts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/insights/configure-datasets#analyze-object-contexts).

**Cluster Toolkit**

Feature

Cluster Toolkit v1.106.0 is available. This release adds support for flexible managed instance groups on [static compute nodes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cluster-toolkit/docs/slurm/manage-static-nodes), multiple network interfaces (multi-NIC) for Google Cloud Managed Lustre instances, and parallelism controls for Terraform to accelerate cluster deployment and teardown.

This release also introduces the `cloud-build` community module to build container images with Cloud Build.

Additionally, this release adds preflight checks for storage profiles when you [submit jobs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cluster-toolkit/docs/reference/gcluster-job-submit) and cleans up gateways when you [cancel jobs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cluster-toolkit/docs/reference/gcluster-job-cancel).

This update also scopes the `--main-only` flag in the [`gcluster job logs` command](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cluster-toolkit/docs/reference/gcluster-job-logs) to the main Pod and its default container.

For more information, see the [release announcement on GitHub](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cluster-toolkit/discussions/6467).

**Compute Engine**

Feature

**Generally available** : You can query regional views of global Compute Engine project and OS image resources by using the regional read-only `projectViews` and `imageViews` endpoints. Querying regional views isolates your control-plane read requests to a specific region, helping your workloads stay available during global API disruptions. For more information, see [Use regional views for resilient control-plane reads](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/architecture/regional-views-global-resources) and [Access global resources regionally for high availability](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/architecture/access-global-resources-regionally).
